title: Add RBACv2 approval gates with KMS residency quarantine and compact audit bridge
author: Ana Morales
release_notes: Introduce RBACv2 approval gates for cross-region KMS usage; new quarantine mode for requests that fail residency checks; compact audit bridge returns lightweight proofs for compliance ingestion.
description: Motivation: Several customers and compliance auditors requested a tighter control path for operator-driven cross-region key usage and clearer audit artifacts that are compact enough to be forwarded to long-term archives without leaking sensitive payloads. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) RBACv2 approval gates that require a secondary operator approval for KMS operations which would violate a tenant's declared residency; 2) a KMS residency quarantine mode which short-circuits risky requests to a quarantine queue instead of failing them outright; and 3) a compact audit bridge that emits verifiable, pseudonymized proofs (hash + metadata) suitable for compliance retention stores. Summary of changes: - Introduced a new RBAC policy predicate operator.residency_approval_needed and a decision hook in authz that flips to an approval-required state when a request's requested_kms_region != tenant.allowed_regions and the request matches sensitive data flags. - Added an approval service (operator-approval) that supports approve/reject with TTL-based ephemeral grants; grants are represented as approval tokens bound to request IDs and operators. - Implemented quarantine flow: requests flagged for quarantine are routed to a quarantine queue (quarantine/v1) with backoff and a bounded retry window; quarantined requests produce a retention-safe audit envelope and are visible in the Console under Security -> Quarantine. - Compact audit bridge: new bridge service (audit-compact) which accepts audit envelopes and outputs a small proof object (sha256 over canonicalized envelope + kms_region_tag + policy_fingerprint) and an encrypted reference pointer for the original envelope stored in the audit vault; the bridge publishes proofs to the existing audit-forwarder with a residency tag. - Migration: feature is behind a controlled rollout flag (rbacv2.residency_approval). The PR includes a migrator that creates default policy templates and a CLI command for operators to bulk-accept outstanding quarantine items after review. - Tests: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests for approval token lifecycle, e2e flow test that simulates a tenant with single-region residency and attempts a cross-region KMS wrap; added basic load test for quarantine queue consumer. Checklist: - [x] Policy schema changes and templates - [x] Approval service and token lifecycle - [x] Quarantine queue + backoff/retry policy - [x] Compact audit bridge + vault integration shim - [x] Console UI stubs for Quarantine view - [x] Integration & e2e tests - [x] Documentation draft for ops runbook Migration notes and operational considerations: - The approval tokens are ephemeral and TTL-bound. Tokens are signed by the operator-approval service and validated by authz middleware. Existing operator roles will need the new 'residency-approver' template to create tokens. - Quarantine queue size and retention policies should be provisioned before enabling the feature in production; recommended retention default is 72 hours. - The compact audit bridge requires the audit vault to expose a write-only S3 bucket and an envelope encryption key; migration includes a dry-run mode where full envelopes are stored alongside proofs for 30 days. - Performance: path adds ~15ms median to KMS-bound requests that transit the authz approval check when the feature flag is on. The quarantine fast-path has negligible latency impact for non-quarantined requests. Security rationale: This approach minimizes silent cross-region key usage by introducing operator visibility and explicit consent windows while preserving availability by routing risky requests to quarantine rather than failing them. The compact audit proofs avoid storing tenant input in the compliance index while retaining verifiability. Related work: ENG-2801 (residency tagging), ENG-3340 (audit-forwarder refactor), SRE-892 (quarantine operators runbook).

review_comments: Michael Chen: The approval token must be scoped to request ID and operator ID — otherwise we risk token reuse across requests. Please add explicit audience claims and a nonce. (requested changes)
Ana Morales (author): Added nonce and audience fields to token structure and updated validation code. See commit 4b8d3c9. (reply)
Priya Nair: The quarantine retention default of 72h seems low for some regulated customers. Can we make this configurable per-tenant and add a warning in the Console? (requested changes)
Ana Morales: Made retention configurable via tenancy config and added a warning banner to the Console stub. (reply)
Jonas Feld: The audit-compact proof composition should include the policy fingerprint and a residency tag. Also include test vectors for the proof generator. (requested changes)
Ana Morales: Included policy_fingerprint and residency_tag in the proof payload; added unit test vectors and a verification helper in tests. (reply)
SRE CI Bot: Load test showed quarantine consumer can fall behind at 5k/s in region-us-west under peak — recommend autoscale settings in the runbook. (comment)
Ana Morales: Adjusted consumer autoscale suggestion and added a note to the runbook. (reply)
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge. PR cleaned up feature flags and added changelog entry in CHANGELOG.md.
changelog_entry: Security: RBACv2 residency approval gates + KMS quarantine and compact audit proofs (feature-flagged).
notes: This PR is part of a staged rollout. On-call teams will be notified when the rollout crosses the 50% tenancy threshold. A follow-up PR will add tenant-level policy templates and a GraphQL index for quarantine analytics.
